consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... she has astigmatism, which means her eyes don't focus properly on things. It's been a challenge for her, especially when trying to read or watch TV. We're really worried about how this might affect her learning.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She had fluid in her ear for a while, and we were so scared it would affect her hearing permanently. Luckily, after treatment, everything seems back to normal now. But I still get anxious whenever she complains about her ear.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has been an issue for her since she started eating solid foods. Some foods are just too hard for her to manage. We've had to adjust her diet accordingly to make sure she can eat comfortably.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist says she needs regular check-ups to monitor her heart health. I try to stay on top of these appointments because I know how crucial they are for her well-being. It's always a relief when the results come back normal.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, she's been slower than her peers to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting. It was worrying at first, but with therapy and support, she's making progress. I'm just eager for her to catch up.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food textures can be a real issue for her. She's very picky and will only eat certain things if they're prepared in specific ways. Mealtime can be challenging, but we're learning to navigate her preferences.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... two main concerns. Firstly, her fontanelle took longer than usual to close completely. And secondly, her speech development isn't where it should be for her age. She doesn't speak as much as other children her age. Both these things worry me and I hope we can find ways to support her better.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular check-ups to monitor her heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with food textures and is very picky, eating only certain foods prepared in specific ways, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including slower progress in reaching milestones like walking or sitting, and speech development that is not on par with her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay is reported in almost all children with the condition.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had fluid in her ear, which was treated, and now her hearing seems back to normal.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, affecting her ability to focus on things, especially when reading or watching TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with chewing and managing certain foods due to their hardness.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important. Regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's learning is affected by her vision and possibly her hearing issues, as well as developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and speech development issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle took longer than usual to close completely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups
* Regular hearing reviews
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Check position of testes in boys
* Consider a palate review
* Referral for a cardiac review
* Consider a skeletal review
* Monitor growth velocity
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher-than-normal curvature of her cornea. This affects how she sees objects at different distances. She sometimes struggles with focusing, especially when looking at things close-up. 

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child had fluid buildup in her ears a couple of times. It affected her ability to hear clearly and caused discomfort. Thankfully, after treatment‚ it cleared up‚ but we monitor her ears regularly now.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth seem prone to chipping or breaking easier than they should. Even minor accidents can cause noticeable damage‚ so we have to ensure she’s extra careful during meals and playtime to avoid any incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Compared to other kids‚ she tires out faster during physical activities. While she can run around and have fun‚ we notice she needs breaks sooner than her friends do. It might be related to her overall energy levels rather than a specific heart condition‚ but we keep an eye on it.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she falls more frequently than other children her age. Whether it’s due to coordination or balance issues‚ we’re working with her to improve strength and agility to reduce these incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been challenging for her since infancy. Certain textures and tastes make mealtime difficult‚ and she has sensitivities to particular foods that trigger digestive discomfort.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned issues‚ our child moves slightly differently compared to her peers. There’s also a concern regarding delayed fontanelle closure‚ where certain bones in her skull took longer to fully close than typically expected. These aspects require periodic assessments to monitor progress and adjust care accordingly.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out faster during physical activities and may have a heart condition, although the specifics are not detailed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had feeding difficulties since infancy, with challenges related to certain textures and tastes, and sensitivities to particular foods that trigger digestive discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more frequently than other children her age, possibly due to coordination or balance issues, and has a history of delayed fontanelle closure.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had fluid buildup in her ears, which affected her ability to hear clearly and caused discomfort, but it has been treated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects how she sees objects at different distances, and sometimes struggles with focusing, especially when looking at things close-up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem prone to chipping or breaking easier than they should, even with minor accidents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and may have coordination or balance issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delays, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a concern regarding delayed fontanelle closure and moves slightly differently compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, or curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent chipping or breaking.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for any hearing loss or ear problems.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for any vision problems.
* Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor for any heart conditions.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and coordination issues.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular assessments to monitor progress and adjust care accordingly for the patient's specific needs.

Parent: Actually, we've noticed he often squints when trying to focus on things. It's like his eyes get tired easily, and he has trouble seeing clearly unless he's really close to what he's looking at.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, he does turn the TV volume up very high to hear it properly. We're not sure if it's a hearing issue or just a preference‚ but it's definitely something we've observed over time.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: He complains about tooth sensitivity‚ especially with cold foods or drinks. It's become a bit of an issue because he loves ice cream and cold milk‚ but they seem to cause him discomfort.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There is a valve abnormality that was detected during one of our check-ups. So far‚ it hasn't seemed to affect his daily life significantly‚ but we do keep an eye on it through regular appointments.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Coordination seems to be a bit of a challenge for him. When he tries to run or perform physical activities‚ he appears less coordinated than his peers. It's subtle‚ but noticeable.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: His weight gain has been slower compared to other kids his age. We're watching his diet and ensuring he gets enough nutrients‚ but so far‚ it remains a concern.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the issues already mentioned‚ he also has a speech delay and was diagnosed with hip dysplasia. These have been significant challenges for us‚ and we're working closely with therapists and specialists to address them.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality that was detected during a check-up, which so far hasn't seemed to affect his daily life significantly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's weight gain has been slower compared to other kids his age, and his parents are watching his diet and ensuring he gets enough nutrients.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination challenges, appearing less coordinated than his peers when performing physical activities, and has been diagnosed with speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and many have developmental delay and behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing issues, turning the TV volume up very high to hear it properly, and has been diagnosed with speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on things, has trouble seeing clearly unless he's really close to what he's looking at, and has been diagnosed with hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity, especially with cold foods or drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and coordination challenges, which may impact his educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination challenges, speech delay, and has been diagnosed with hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor valve abnormality
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal concerns
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address coordination challenges, speech delay, and behavioural differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires close monitoring and periodic visits to the cardiologist, managed with medication and lifestyle adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties that affect daily routine and nutrition intake, making mealtimes stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears to get tired more quickly than peers during physical activities, suggesting a potential neurodevelopmental aspect.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient frequently asks people to repeat themselves, indicating potential hearing issues, especially in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often complains of squinting when trying to focus on objects or text, suggesting a vision issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with some requiring patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring extra precautions and regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed fontanelle closure and short fingers, which are under regular observation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent further damage.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing concerns.
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems and provide appropriate correction.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess bone health.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address specific challenges.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected for a child of his age and health, particularly when playing or running around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than you'd expect for a child of his age and health when playing or running around, indicating a need for close monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble eating certain foods and sometimes shows discomfort after eating, with varying severity from day to day.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, requiring close management with neurologists to adjust medications and recognize signs of upcoming seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks to have things repeated because he didn't catch them the first time, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, for which he wears glasses, helping to address the challenge, particularly in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go to the dentist more often than most kids due to frequent dental problems despite good home care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is taking a bit longer to hit developmental milestones compared to other kids his age, requiring close monitoring and discussion with specialists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally delayed, taking longer to hit milestones, and has epilepsy, which impacts his daily life and requires management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental issues promptly.
* Hearing reviews to age 5, even if earlier reviews give a clear response, to catch any potential hearing loss early.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor and correct vision problems.
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis, to assess heart condition.
* Monitor growth velocity, and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental delays and other challenges.
* Close monitoring and management of epilepsy with neurologists.
* Regular check-ups with specialists to address feeding difficulties and gastrointestinal issues.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition involving one of the valves, which is monitored by a specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, including trouble swallowing and frequent vomiting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems clumsy, trips over her own feet, and has delayed development, which may be related to her overall neurological development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, frequently asking for repetition and not responding to softer voices.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes frequently, especially when trying to focus, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth that stick out, causing concern for the parent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient started talking later than most children and seems behind her peers in terms of development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed development and speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved 5th fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and enamel health.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to assess for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to check for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for skeletal anomalies.
* Speech therapy to address speech delay.
* Occupational therapy and physiotherapy to support developmental delays.
* Behavioral therapy to address any behavioral differences or concerns.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's heartbeat seems faster than expected, especially after physical activity.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with food textures, avoiding specific foods due to their texture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences brief episodes of staring off into space, which seem to pass without warning signs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing certain sounds or following conversations in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurry vision, especially when trying to read or watch TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require frequent maintenance due to a propensity for cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a subtle posture issue, with a noticeable deviation from a straight posture when standing or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address the patient's propensity for cavities.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue with their heart.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky with food textures and some things he just won't eat because of how they feel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to hear some sounds but not others clearly, especially with background noise.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things look blurry sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than usual front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to make himself understood when speaking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and potential need for glasses or other treatment.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and adjust treatment as necessary.
* Neurological monitoring to manage the patient's epilepsy and adjust medication as necessary.
* Speech therapy to help the patient improve their communication skills.
* Occupational therapy to help the patient with feeding and food texture issues.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty keeping up with peers during prolonged physical activities and gets winded easily, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiac issues, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, are reported in approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel movement issues, including constipation and diarrhea, which require dietary adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and gastrointestinal issues, such as lack of interest in feeding, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epilepsy, which is managed with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient frequently asks for repetitions due to difficulty hearing, especially in both quiet and noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Conductive hearing loss, often due to recurrent otitis media or glue ear, is a common feature, and many individuals require regular hearing checks and potential interventions like grommet insertions.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints when trying to focus, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, are more common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and avoids certain foods due to chewing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns, including large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental issues, are common, necessitating regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream schools and others requiring special education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and anxiety, are common, and may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curvature of the 5th fingers, and potential issues like scoliosis or hip dysplasia, are features of KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect and manage hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate cardiac function.
* Consideration of a palate review, especially if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.
* Regular monitoring and management of epilepsy.
* Dietary adjustments to regulate bowel movements.
* Regular check-ups for potential palatal abnormalities and their impact on speech and feeding.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other children, which has been observed during physical activities or even after short walks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, making meal times challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and difficulty making himself understood when trying to communicate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to hear some sounds but not others clearly, and has instances where he responds to loud noises but doesn't react to softer ones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than usual front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty making himself understood when trying to communicate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess the patient's vision.
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to assess the patient's heart health.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor the patient's skeletal development.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and communication.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected for their age when playing, which requires monitoring to prevent overexertion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected for their age when playing, suggesting potential cardiac concerns that need monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, some of which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with eating and swallowing food, making meal times challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced delayed milestones, such as sitting and walking, and has noticeable speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated in noisy environments, suggesting potential hearing or sensory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, requiring glasses to correct vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods, requiring adaptations to make mealtime easier.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups, sometimes with a specialist SEN dentist.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and is working with therapists to address this issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced delayed milestones and has noticeable speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems.
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess cardiac health.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and speech concerns.
* Adapt mealtime strategies to make eating and swallowing easier for the patient.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires regular monitoring by a cardiologist to assess its impact on overall health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties during mealtimes, getting frustrated when eating, which affects her mood.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a few needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears less coordinated compared to peers, with simple tasks requiring balance and movement seeming to challenge her more.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond right away when called, seeming preoccupied or distracted, and has required more frequent dental check-ups and cleanings to prevent problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple grommet insertions and some needing hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus, with her eyes seeming to get tired easily, and having trouble seeing clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require more attention than usual, with the dentist recommending more frequent check-ups and cleanings to prevent problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, with careful brushing being very important and regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, but the extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, leading some to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to express herself in a way that others understand, leading to frustration during interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate, and most having some degree of developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably shorter fingers than usual.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, with many having short fingers and a curvature of the 5th fingers, and a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to prevent and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to monitor the septal defect.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for spinal and skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental and behavioural challenges.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition involving a valve not being right.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky about what she eats and doesn't like certain textures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids her age and has trouble talking clearly sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really frustrated when it's too loud and has astigmatism.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which makes it hard for her to see clearly sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and large front teeth, and some have other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit behind other children her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids her age and has trouble talking clearly sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage or chipping.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to monitor for astigmatism and other vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor for heart conditions.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address developmental delays.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires monitoring and potential treatment as she grows older.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences digestive issues and discomfort after eating, leading to frustration during mealtimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally experiences brief episodes where she stares off into space and seems completely unresponsive for a few seconds, and has difficulty articulating thoughts into speech.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to pick up on certain sounds but struggles with others, and has trouble responding to quieter noises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often rubs her eyes, especially when trying to focus on something close up, and has trouble adjusting to different distances.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are somewhat brittle and tend to break or chip more easily than expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty articulating thoughts into speech and has occasional episodes of unresponsiveness.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's brittle teeth and prevent further damage.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's septal defect and discuss potential treatment options.
* Referral for speech therapy to address the patient's difficulty articulating thoughts into speech.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition and requires regular heart check-ups to monitor everything and ensure it's functioning properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences slower weight gain compared to his peers, which could indicate some issue with digestion or absorption of nutrients.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, which are distressing for him and his family.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported as having seizures, of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV up very high to hear it clearly, suggesting he might be having some difficulty with his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often complains that things appear blurry to him, which can get frustrating during school lessons or when watching TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods like meat or crunchy vegetables, suggesting his teeth or jaw aren't strong enough yet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's physical movements and coordination seem a bit off compared to other kids his age, and he struggles with balance or running smoothly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and the degree of delay ranges from mild to severe, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as typical children, and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and jaw development
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and potential vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition
* Consider referral for a skeletal review to assess the patient's spinal bones and potential skeletal anomalies
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any developmental delays
* Monitor the patient's growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise, especially if sacral dimple is present

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in her heart, which is being monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's weight gain has been slower compared to her peers, and her parents are keeping an eye on her eating habits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of unusual staring or blank spells, which can be alarming at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often turns the volume of the TV up very high, which makes her parents worry about her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit very close to the TV or when reading books, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist frequently due to various tooth issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a speech delay, which is being addressed through therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address tooth issues
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Speech therapy to address speech delay
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and behaviour.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes she seems to pick up on certain sounds but then ignores others even when they're really loud. It's almost as if she's tuning in and out of conversations or noises around her. We're not sure if it's a hearing issue or just her way of dealing with too much stimulation.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth have weak enamel, which worries us because it makes them more prone to cavities and decay. We make sure to brush them regularly and visit the dentist often to keep an eye on the situation.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, the doctors have mentioned that she needs regular check-ups for her heart because of a pre-existing condition. These appointments help monitor everything and ensure nothing unexpected comes up.

Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, she's been slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting. While her peers were already doing these things with ease, she took a bit longer to master them. We're working closely with her therapists to support her development.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A

Parent: N/A

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular check-ups to monitor and ensure nothing unexpected comes up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, making mealtime challenging, and there are certain foods she won't touch, making it tricky to get her to eat a balanced diet. She also has palatal abnormalities that the doctors keep an eye on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, taking longer to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting. She also has balance issues, stumbling or losing balance more easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe. Around 20-40% of people are reported as having seizures, of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to have hearing issues, sometimes picking up on certain sounds but then ignoring others, even when they're really loud.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means she has trouble seeing things clearly because her eyes don't focus properly together.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, making her teeth more prone to cavities and decay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and balance issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety. Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has balance issues and stumbles or loses balance more easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's weak enamel and prevent cavities and decay.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns.
* Regular eyesight (ophthalmology) reviews to monitor the patient's astigmatism and address any concerns.
* Regular check-ups for the patient's pre-existing heart condition.
* Consider referral for a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) if not already done.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor the patient's skeletal development.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if the patient's height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any concerns.
