# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Physical activities are challenging for her. She can't keep up with her friends during long periods of play or sports.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Her weight gain has been slower compared to other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: She experiences epilepsy. We monitor her condition closely and work with her doctors to manage it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: Loud noises seem to overwhelm her. She gets frustrated in crowded or noisy areas, like malls or playgrounds.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: She has myopia. It's been noticeable since she started school, and it affects her ability to see the board clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Chewing can be difficult for her, especially with tougher foods like meats or hard fruits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: She has a slightly different gait pattern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to monitor vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor skeletal health
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any concerns.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks people to repeat themselves because she didn't quite catch what they said the first time, indicating some hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and uses glasses to correct her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges with chewing harder foods and tends to avoid those types of food or takes smaller bites.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has been diagnosed with hypermetropia, which means he has a higher than average curvature of the cornea. This causes some issues with his vision and we're working on correcting it with glasses and possibly surgery in the future. We've noticed it affects his ability to focus on distant objects.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, he had a glue ear last year which affected his hearing temporarily. Fortunately, after treatment and time to heal, his hearing returned to normal. However, we do monitor his ear health closely now due to the history of this condition.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Lately, our child has complaned about tooth sensitivity when consuming cold foods or drinks. It seems to cause him significant discomfort and pain. We've taken him to see a dentist who suggested a few possible reasons and treatments to alleviate this symptom.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Unfortunately, during a routine check-up, a septal defect was discovered in his heart. The cardioligist explained it's a hole between the chambers of the heart that didn't close the way it should after birth. We're currently exploring options for corrective surgery and managing the situation closely with medication and lifestyle adjustments.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Observing our child's physical development and coordination skills, we've noticed he seems less coordinated when performing certain movements compared to peers of the same age. While it might not be a severe concern at this stage, we believe monitoring and possibly seeking occupational therapy could help improve these skills over time.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Interestingly, our child often shows a preference against eating specific types of food which sometimes leads to mealtime struggles. Despite offering a variet of healthy options, he tends to stick to a limited range of foods he finds acceptable. This can be challenging but we manage by ensuring nutritional balance through supplements when necessary.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: One notable feature is that our child has shorter fingers than average which can affect dexterity and fine motor skills. While not causing significant daily issues at this point, understanding and accommodating this difference will be important as he grows and engages in more complex activities.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect, a hole between the chambers of the heart that didn't close the way it should after birth, requiring corrective surgery and management with medication and lifestyle adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, showing a preference against eating specific types of food, leading to mealtime struggles, and requiring nutritional balance through supplements when necessary.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a lack of interest in feeding being significant and long-lasting in some cases.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has less coordination when performing certain movements compared to peers of the same age, potentially benefiting from occupational therapy to improve these skills over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear which affected his hearing temporarily, but after treatment and time to heal, his hearing returned to normal, with ongoing monitoring of ear health due to the history of this condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple aeration tube insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some needing hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, a higher than average curvature of the cornea, causing issues with vision and potentially requiring correction with glasses and possibly surgery in the future.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint, with treatment including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has tooth sensitivity when consuming cold foods or drinks, causing significant discomfort and pain, with possible treatments to alleviate this symptom.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, with careful brushing being very important, and regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most going to a mainstream primary school, but some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has less coordination and potentially benefits from occupational therapy, and has feeding difficulties and preferences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication possibly being appropriate in some circumstances, and developmental delay being reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than average, which can affect dexterity and fine motor skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number having hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and overall dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor for any signs of hearing loss or glue ear.
* Eyesight review to monitor and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the septal defect and determine the best course of treatment.
* Consideration of occupational therapy to improve coordination and fine motor skills.
* Monitoring of feeding difficulties and adjustments to ensure nutritional balance.
* Regular monitoring of ear health due to the history of glue ear.
* Consideration of corrective surgery for the septal defect.
* Ongoing monitoring and management of the patient's heart condition with medication and lifestyle adjustments.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily, even when playing with kids her own age, and simple games can leave her breathless and needing a break.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily, even when playing with kids her own age, and simple games can leave her breathless and needing a break.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: As a baby, feeding was challenging, with trouble latching on and often spitting up, although this has improved significantly over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Physical activities exhaust her quicker than her peers, and she needs to sit down after a short while.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: Loud noises seem to overwhelm her, and she gets frustrated in crowded or noisy areas.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: She often rubs her eyes, especially when she's trying to focus on something, and it's almost like she's straining to see clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Her front teeth are noticeably larger than those of her friends.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: She moves a bit differently compared to other kids her age, and it's subtle but noticeable when she's running or climbing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: She moves a bit differently compared to other kids her age, and it's subtle but noticeable when she's running or climbing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to check for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to check for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to check for skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and behaviour.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve abnormality.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky about what he eats and sometimes leaves food on his plate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really tired during physical activity and needs to rest after a while. He also struggles with clarity when trying to talk, and sometimes his sentences don't make sense.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient doesn't always respond when called, and his parents have to repeat themselves multiple times. He also squints when looking at things.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints when looking at things.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been complaining about tooth sensitivity, especially with cold food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with clarity when trying to talk, and sometimes his sentences don't make sense.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and some have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor for heart valve abnormalities
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for spinal and skeletal abnormalities
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and behaviour
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
